'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****[[Government of Afghanistan|Government]] forces and the [[Taliban]] clash in [[Herat]], the [[provinces of Afghanistan|provincial]] capital of [[Herat Province]], where the [[Islamist]] group has seized many [[districts of Afghanistan|districts]]. The Taliban also captures adjoining border crossings with [[Iran]] and [[Turkmenistan]] as the [[United Nations]] accuses them of killing a [[United Nations]] serviceman yesterday during an attack on a UN compound. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210731-taliban-and-afghan-forces-clash-again-outside-herat-city (France 24)]
****The Taliban enters [[Kandahar]] as intense fighting is reported in three major [[list of cities in Afghanistan|cities]]. Kandahar MP spokesman Gul Ahmad Kamin says that the fighting there is the worst that has been seen in 20 years, with the Taliban seeking to establish their temporary capital there. Kamin also says that the situation is worsening "hour by hour" as he warns that if Kandahar falls, five or six other provinces in the region would also be captured by the Taliban. It is also reported that the Taliban made rapid major gains in rural areas. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58040141 (BBC News)]
*[[Sinai insurgency]]
**Eight soldiers are killed by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Sinai Province|ISIL]] during anti-terrorism operations in northern [[Sinai Peninsula|Sinai]], [[Egypt]]. Eighty-nine ISIL militants are also killed. Arms and ammunitions are confiscated, while hundreds of explosive devices, some explosive belts, thirteen tunnel entrances and 200 arms-loaded vehicles are destroyed. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/1/egypt-eight-troops-killed-in-sinai-anti-terrorism-operations (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**The deputy governor of [[Al Bayda Governorate]] says that [[Houthi movement|Houthi]] [[insurgent]]s have taken control of Naman and Nateh [[list of districts of Yemen|districts]], [[internally displaced person|displacing]] many civilians. [https://www.thedefensepost.com/2021/07/30/houthis-al-bayda-province/ (''The Defense Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Thirty-three people are dead during a collision between a fuel truck and a crowded bus in Kibuba, [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/2/dozens-killed-in-fuel-truck-accident-in-dr-congo (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Tokyo]] reports a record 4,058 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, while the number of new cases across [[Japan]] reaches a record 12,341. [https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/summer/officials-tokyo-alarmed-virus-cases-record-highs-1.6125470 (CBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Laos]]
****[[Laos]] reports a record 380 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 6,299. [https://laotiantimes.com/2021/07/31/laos-reaches-over-6000-cases-of-covid-19-as-imported-cases-surge/ (''The Laotian Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 17,786 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,113,272. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/07/31/covid-19-17786-cases-on-saturday-july-31. (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] reports its first five cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Epsilon variant]] in [[Lahore]], which was originally detected in [[California]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1637879 (DAWN)]
****[[Sindh]] province imposes a partial [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in [[Pakistan]]'s largest city of [[Karachi]] in order to reduce the spread of the highly contagious [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. The lockdown is in effect until August 8. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/delta-variant-spread-forces-partial-lockdown-on-karachi-pakistan-s-largest-city-101627655970639.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 18,912 new cases and 178 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 597,287 and the nationwide death toll to 4,857. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/thailand-reports-daily-record-of-18912-new-covid-19-cases (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in El Salvador]]
****[[El Salvador]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.617|Lineage B.1.617]] Delta variant, which was originally detected in [[India]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-el-salvador/el-salvador-detects-first-case-of-covid-19-delta-variant-health-minister-idUSKBN2F10PG (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
*****[[Florida]] reports a record 21,683 cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, surpassing the previous record of 19,334 cases reported on January 7. [https://www.tampabay.com/news/health/2021/07/31/florida-sets-coronavirus-daily-case-record-according-to-cdc/ (''Tampa Bay Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Argentina]]
***Health minister [[Carla Vizzotti]] reports that [[Argentina]] has applied nearly 32 million doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. Argentina has so far reported 4.9 million cases and over 105,000 deaths from COVID-19. [http://www.cndigital.com.ar/noticias/54362_los-tres-objetivos-que-marcan-la-hoja-de-ruta-del-gobierno-para-garantizar-la-vacunacion.html (CNDigital)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Brisbane]] and surrounding towns enter a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] after an increase in the number of new COVID-19 cases linked to the ongoing cluster in [[New South Wales]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jul/31/queensland-covid-lockdown-enormous-number-of-hotspots-expected-after-six-new-cases (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Réunion]]
***Amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases, the [[French overseas territory]] of [[Réunion]] enters a two-week partial lockdown which restricts the movement of people to {{cvt|10|km}} during the day and {{cvt|5|km}} on Sunday as well as closing all cafés, restaurants and gyms. A curfew is also being imposed between 6 p.m. and 5 a.m. when movement is not allowed except for essential reasons. [https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210729-partial-lockdown-announced-on-reunion-island-as-covid-cases-surge (France 24)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**As the six-month anniversary of the military coup against civilian leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] approaches, protests occur in [[Mandalay]] with university students waving flags and saying that there is "no possibility of dialogue" with the junta. The junta says that former civilian leaders are spreading "biased information". [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/protests-accusations-against-myanmar-junta-ahead-coup-anniversary-2021-07-31/ (Reuters)]
*[[Madagascar]] President [[Andry Rajoelina]] calls on the military to take "responsibility for threats to national sovereignty and threats to national security" after a plot to assassinate him was foiled last week. Rajoelina called on the new military graduates to uphold democracy. [https://madagascar-tribune.com/Andry-Rajoelina-appelle-les-militaires-a-prendre-leurs-responsabilites.html (''Madagascar Tribune'')]
